purpose: A curated, traceable visual benchmark for Medical Emoji proposal artwork. This dataset is descriptive and does not establish that artwork alone caused encoding.

source_register.name: Unicode Emoji Proposals chart
source_register.outcome_definition: Each record is listed by Unicode as the proposal source for one or more encoded emoji.

copyright_policy: Records point to public official documents. Third-party artwork is not copied into this repository.

records.relevance: Direct anatomical-organ precedent; useful for color, silhouette, and internal-structure comparison.
records.image_evidence: Color sample visible on page 1; the proposal says black-and-white images were pending, so it must not be treated as current-format compliant.

records.relevance: Direct anatomical-organ precedent; the paired lobes and trachea provide a strong non-bean silhouette.
records.image_evidence: Color sample visible on page 1. It predates the current four-sample requirement and is historical context only.

records.relevance: Closest successful medical-concept comparator; the visible color and black-and-white samples show a paradigm that survives a monochrome treatment.
records.image_evidence: Color and black-and-white reference samples are visible on page 1; the exact 18x18/72x72 placement must be verified in the original PDF before using it as a format precedent.

records.relevance: Primary confusability comparator for a single bean-shaped candidate silhouette.
records.image_evidence: Three color proposal alternatives are visible on page 1. The proposal page does not show the present-day four-sample layout.

records.relevance: Useful contrast case: a compact radial silhouette needs a small number of high-salience cues rather than anatomical detail.
records.image_evidence: Sample and alternate illustrations are visible on page 1. This is a historical visual comparison, not a current-format template.

records.relevance: A second food-shape comparator; leaves and a tapered root are cues that separate it from a generic round or bean form.
records.image_evidence: Color and black-and-white candidate art is visible on page 1. Verify exact native-size samples in the original PDF if it is used for a formal layout comparison.

records.relevance: Tests whether a concept can retain its defining structural cue in monochrome; useful for assessing black-and-white variants with a line-based defining feature.
records.image_evidence: Black-and-white and color examples are visible on page 1. The samples are evidence of a clear defining cue, not a prescription for organ art.

records.relevance: Best current-format comparator in this seed set: the first page visibly presents 18x18 and 72x72 examples in color and black-and-white.
records.image_evidence: All four size-and-mode samples are visible in a 2x2 grid on page 1. It demonstrates that the critical 18x18 signal is an unmistakable silhouette, not accumulated internal detail.

records.relevance: A useful object precedent: the proposal limits visual contents to gold coins because other contents become muddled at small resolutions.
records.image_evidence: 72px and 18px color samples are visible on page 1. It is a useful small-detail lesson but not a complete present-day format example.

records.relevance: Shows a successful abstract paradigm where directional mass movement, rather than literal detail, carries recognition at 18px.
records.image_evidence: 72px and 18px color samples are visible on page 1. Its historical value is its simplification strategy, not a direct anatomical comparison.
